narrative: The model estimates a 14% chance that you will fail, which means passing is the strongly likely outcome, not failure. Because of that, the explanation does not support saying the model predicted you will fail or that remedial courses are automatically justified. The three most influential factors all pushed toward passing. Your record of no past class failures was the strongest factor and matches the passers’ average. The quality of your family relationships was next; most passers report good relationships, as you do. The reason you chose the school—its reputation—was third and is also common among passers. Practically, the model sees you as likely to pass. To improve further, keep attendance steady—your two absences are below the passers’ average of 3.78—maintain regular study time, ask for help early if a subject becomes difficult, and keep using family support. If remedial courses are still required, ask the school what rule or additional evidence triggered that requirement, because this prediction alone—a 14% fail probability with all top factors pointing toward passing—does not explain mandatory remediation.
